messages:
kyle: Quick sync — we need to finalize the rollout plan for integrating FlashAttention v2/v3 into runtime. primary concerns: kernel selector heuristics, batching effects on latency P95, and KV cache semantics when switching kernels mid-session.

maria: +1. I captured some new perf diffs from the nightly: FAv3 gives ~18% token throughput win on A100 for short seqs but regresses 3-6% on long seqs with paged-Attn. attaching a link to the perf dashboard: <http://perf.internal/runs/2026-03-10/FAv2-vs-FAv3>

tony: Re: KV cache — the change in memory layout for FAv3 caused an extra memcpy in our current KV wrapper. That's the main source of the long sequence regression. I prototyped lazy-views to avoid copies, numbers look promising.

sophie: Can you drop the prototype snippet here, tony? I want to validate with our paging tests.

tony: Sure — minimal example:
```
// avoid memcpy by creating a view into kv tensor
auto kv_view = kv_tensor.as_strided(shape, stride);
// kernel call
flashv3::attn_forward(q,kv_view, ...);
```
This preserves alignment for the fused kernels.

maria: Nice. Also noticed batching heuristics need tweak: FAv3 increases compute variance, so our current static batch size cap (batch_max_tokens=4096) is not optimal. We should make batch cap a function of seq distribution.

kyle: Proposal: feature-flag rollout with three phases
1) opt-in perf test fleet (fflag: attn_fa3_test) — small % traffic, run profiling hooks
2) canary with KV layout fallback (attn_fa3_canary) — switch to FAv3 but if memcpy detected fallback to FAv2
3) gradual ramp with telemetry gating (attn_fa3_ramp).

maria: Important: telemetry must capture per-request kernel chosen, batch size, seq_len, kv_copy_bytes. Add these as tags so we can pivot fast.

infra-bot: Reminder: when toggling fflags on Dedicated clusters, include node labels for A100 vs H100; kernel selection differs by arch.

tony: For gating, I'd add an automatic rollback rule: if 5-minute P95 latency increases >7% OR token cost >10% for the canary group, roll back.

sophie: On the paging tests: I ran a 2k user sim with mixed seqs. With the lazy-view approach, P95 improved for long tails, but tail variance increased slightly for short seqs. We should test hybrid: prefer FAv3 for seq<=512, FAv2 for seq>512, and allow runtime to remap mid-session if KV compatible.

kyle: Hybrid selector sounds sensible. Action items:
- tony: finalize lazy-view patch and open PR with tests (due EOD tomorrow)
- maria: add telemetry metrics & dashboard panels (due +2d)
- sophie: run hybrid sim and add results to the runbook (due +3d)
- infra: add fflags and canary groups, ensure H100/A100 labels (estimate +1d)

maria: Also need to update rollout notes in console: explain model-owner knobs (force kernel per-model, per-route overrides).

tony: One open question — how do we handle pinned KV across kernel swaps? If a customer pins a model version that uses FAv2 and we swap to FAv3 in routing, KV binary compatibility could break.

kyle: Decision: do not perform kernel swaps within a pinned model session. Kernel can change only between model-version boundaries. We'll document and enforce this in the selector.

sophie: I'll add a unit test that simulates pinned sessions and ensures the selector refuses mid-session kernel change.

deploy-bot: Deploy plan note: remember to add a dry-run flag for the canary that executes kernels but doesn't serve traffic until all checks pass.

kyle: Good call. Let's reconvene after the PRs land. If any perf regression shows up in canary we'll hit the rollback rule.

maria: I'll post the first perf dashboards once telemetry is live.

kyle: Thanks all — feel free to ping here with links to PR/DCI. :rocket:
